newsitem.title: USA: APRIL's Riaupulp obligated to redeem notes.
newsitem.headline: APRIL's Riaupulp obligated to redeem notes.

text.p: P.T. Riau Andalan Pulp and Paper expects to complete its planned asset sales and therefore is obligated to redeem the outstanding RAPP International Finance notes, company officials told debt holders in a conference call Tuesday.
Called Riaupulp or RAPP, the company is a 98.9 percent held operating subsidiary of the APRIL Group -- Asia Pacific Resources International Holdings Ltd.
Riaupulp Finance Director W. Michael Verge opened the call with a reiteration of the company statement released Friday -- it expects to complete the sales this month and next.
As proposed in March, the company is selling the power plant and chemical manufacturing assets that are part of its paper pulp mill complex in Riau Province, Sumatra, Indonesia.
When the sale was proposed, Riaupulp said the purpose was to provide funds to support expansion and reduce debt and operating costs.
However, Friday's statement said "substantially all the proceeds will be used to pay down indebtedness."
Verge told the conference call the redemption of Riaupulp's secured debt will take the sale proceeds, the company's available cash and an advance from APRIL Group.
Friday, Riaupulp said it expected to complete the sale of the power assets this month for about $270 million and the chemical assets in February for $140 million.

Verge acknowleged Tuesday this was $140 million short of the company's December 31 secured debt of $550 million and said this would be made up with $40 million from land sales and $100 million from cash and unsecured debt.

When analysts pointed out the company's cash position is low right now, he responded "We can't disclose that right now." Then he asked "How did you know?" One analyst noted pulp producers are low on cash at this time.
Verge then said a loan of up to $100 million from APRIL is an option.
The analysts explained noteholders were upset with Riaupulp's redemption plans because 10 year notes were being redeemed so soon after being issued in December 1995.
One said he had paid 105 to 110 for notes that will be redeemed for 101.

Others questioned the speed of the redemption -- no more than 60 days after the sale of the chemical plant -- saying this is "inadequate time to unwind the interest hedges" that accompanied the purchase of the notes.
Verge told the note holders they had "no right to opt out" of the redeemption and Riaupulp has "no obligation to offer (them) a chance" to do that.
However, a lawyer for Franklin Resources Inc, Franklin Templeton Group funds' parent, pointed out the note indenture does allow amendments.
Other noteholders identified during the teleconference were ING Baring, and the Merrill Lynch Global Allocation Fund.
Several participants asked if the companies would consider a meeting with noteholders to discuss changing the indenture.
APRIL Finance Director Barry Kowock said "We will take your thoughts under advisement," adding the conference call "is not the proper forum to discuss" such action.

Asked why holders were not alerted to the possibility the notes would be redeemed when the asset sales were proposed in March, Verge cited the drop in pulp prices since then, explaining this resulted in the sale of the two assets being "a major collateral disposition" under the note indentures.
Friday, Riaupulp said management is evaluating increasing the capacity of the mill to allow it to benefit from expected continued growth for pulp in the Asia Pacific region.
Both finance directors declined to respond to questions about how this redeemption might affect the financing of such an expansion.
Verge did say, in his opening remarks, Riaupulp "must complete (the sale) to stay competitive ... and to finance future expansion."
The two officials also declined to respond to suggestions that the reduced interest payments resulting from the redeemption are part of the savings seen from the asset sales.

Kowock said the prices being received are the "approximate book value" of the assets being sold, adding the amounts were subject to fairness opinions from Merrill Lynch and Co Inc for power plant buyer Riau Prima Energy and SBC Warburg for chemical plant buyer Inti Indorayon Utama PT, Riaupulp's sister company in the APRIL Group.

Friday the company pointed out the sale of the chemical assets is subject to the approval of the public shareholders of Indorayon and is expected to be completed as soon as practicable after such approval.
